summary.title: SPOT-Contact-Single: Improving Single-Sequence-Based Prediction of Protein Contact Map using a Transformer Language Model
summary.authors: Jaspreet Singh, Thomas Litfin, Jaswinder Singh, Kuldip Paliwal, Yaoqi Zhou
summary.executive_summary: This paper introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a novel method for predicting protein contact maps using single-sequence inputs, addressing the limitation of evolutionary-profile-based methods that require homologous sequences. The core innovation is the integration of attention maps from the pre-trained transformer language model ESM-1b as input features, combined with one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs. The model architecture consists of an ensemble of six 12-block ResNet models, trained using both direct contact prediction and distogram-based strategies. The study utilized a large training set of 34,691 proteins from the ProteinNet benchmark, with stringent independent test sets including SPOT-2018 (669 proteins) and CASP14-FM (15 targets). Results demonstrate significant improvements over existing single-sequence predictors like SSCpred, with a 15% improvement in F1-score on the CASP14-FM set. More notably, SPOT-Contact-Single outperforms evolutionary-profile-based methods TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact by 48.7% and 48.5% respectively in F1-score on proteins without homologs (Neff=1). The method is also computationally efficient, being 22 times faster than TrRosetta on CPU. These findings suggest that unsupervised learning features from language models can effectively replace evolutionary information for contact map prediction, particularly for proteins with few homologs, offering a scalable solution for large-scale genomic prediction.

claims.description: SPOT-Contact-Single significantly improves single-sequence-based contact map prediction using ESM-1b attention maps.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a novel method for predicting protein contact maps using single-sequence inputs, addressing the limitation of evolutionary-profile-based methods that require homologous sequences. The core innovation is the integration of attention maps from the pre-trained transformer language model ESM-1b as input features, combined with one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs. The model architecture consists of an ensemble of six 12-block ResNet models, trained using both direct contact prediction and distogram-based strategies. The study utilized a large training set of 34,691 proteins from the ProteinNet benchmark, with stringent independent test sets including SPOT-2018 (669 proteins) and CASP14-FM (15 targets). Results demonstrate significant improvements over existing single-sequence predictors like SSCpred, with a 15% improvement in F1-score on the CASP14-FM set. More notably, SPOT-Contact-Single outperforms evolutionary-profile-based methods TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact by 48.7% and 48.5% respectively in F1-score on proteins without homologs (Neff=1). The method is also computationally efficient, being 22 times faster than TrRosetta on CPU. These findings suggest that unsupervised learning features from language models can effectively replace evolutionary information for contact map prediction, particularly for proteins with few homologs, offering a scalable solution for large-scale genomic prediction.

Research Context
Protein contact map prediction is essential for structure and function prediction. Most existing methods rely on protein-sequence-evolutionary information. Evolutionary profiles may not exist for many proteins. Generating evolutionary profiles is computationally intensive. Single-sequence methods like SSCpred perform poorly compared to MSA-based techniques. Unsupervised deep learning methods inspired by NLP language models have emerged. ESM-1b is an unsupervised method using a Transformer-34 model.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to improve single-sequence-based contact map prediction. The hypothesis is that ESM-1b attention maps can enhance prediction accuracy. The method predicts contact maps without using homologous information. The approach uses an ensemble of residual neural networks. The goal is to outperform single-sequence and MSA-based predictors for low Neff proteins. The study examines the use of ESM-1b's attention map as a feature.

Methodological Details
The training dataset was curated from the ProteinNet benchmark. The dataset consists of 50,914 proteins with high-resolution structures. Proteins were clustered at a 95% sequence identity cut-off. 100 proteins were separated for validation to minimize over-fitting. Homologs were removed using HHblits with an e-value cut-off of 0.1. The final training set contained 34,691 proteins. The validation set contained 88 proteins. The independent test set SPOT-2018 contains 669 proteins. A subset of 46 proteins with Neff=1 formed the Neff1-2018 set. The CASP14-FM test set includes 15 free modelling targets. Input features included one-hot encoding, SPOT-1D-Single outputs, and ESM-1b attention maps. Attention maps were symmetrized and applied average product corrections.

Procedures And Architectures
The neural network architecture was inspired by ResNet. A 12-block ResNet was used as the maximum trainable depth. Convolutional layers had a channel size of 64 and kernel size of 3. Six models were trained with different input feature combinations. Three models predicted contacts as binary classification. Three models predicted inter-residue distances as distance bins. Direct contact models used Binary Cross-Entropy loss. Distogram-based models used Cross-Entropy loss. The Adam optimizer was used with a learning rate of 0.001. The batch size was set to 1. Early stopping was applied with a patience of 3. The ensemble was formed by taking the mean of individual models.

Key Results
SPOT-Contact-Single improved F1-score by 15% over SSCpred on CASP14-FM. The method outperformed TrRosetta by 48.7% in F1-score on Neff=1 proteins. The method outperformed SPOT-Contact by 48.5% in F1-score on Neff=1 proteins. One-hot encoding alone yielded an F1-score of 0.15. Adding SPOT-1D-Single improved F1-score by 22.90%. ESM-1b last-layer attention maps achieved an F1-score of 0.51. This represented a 242% improvement over one-hot encoding. The ensemble achieved a 4% improvement over the second-best individual model. SPOT-Contact-Single achieved an F1-score of 0.32 on Neff=1 proteins. ESM-1b achieved an F1-score of about 0.22 on Neff=1 proteins. SPOT-Contact-Single was 22 times faster than TrRosetta on CPU. SPOT-Contact-Single was 42 times faster than TrRosetta on GPU.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Unsupervised learning features from language models can replace evolutionary information. The method is effective for proteins with few homologs. SPOT-Contact-Single serves as a reasonably accurate screening tool. The method is suitable for large-scale genomic prediction. The use of ESM-1b limits prediction to proteins under 1024 amino acids. Future improvements may involve Transformer or Performer architectures.

Contradictions And Limitations
The method cannot directly predict contact maps for proteins over 1024 amino acids. SPOT-1D-Single is not yet as competitive as evolution-based methods for high Neff. The study relies on the ProteinNet benchmark for training data. The comparison with SSCpred was limited to the CASP14-FM dataset. The method does not employ evolutionary information, limiting its use for high Neff proteins.

Claims
SPOT-Contact-Single significantly improves single-sequence-based contact map prediction using ESM-1b attention maps. The method achieved a 15% improvement in F1-score over SSCpred. It outperformed TrRosetta by 48.7% on Neff=1 proteins. ESM-1b attention maps boosted F1-score to 0.51. The method is limited to proteins under 1024 amino acids. It is not as competitive as evolution-based methods for high Neff proteins. The method offers a faster alternative to evolution-based methods. It is useful for large-scale prediction.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Ablation studies showed ESM-1b attention maps significantly boost performance. Direct contact prediction performed slightly better than distogram-based prediction. The ensemble of six models improved over individual models.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the neural network architecture. Figure 2 shows precision for top predictions. Figure 3 plots F1-score as a function of Neff. Figure 4 shows native and predicted contact-maps. Table 1 describes feature combinations for the ensemble. Table 2 shows feature importance on the validation set. Table 3 compares direct vs distance contact-map prediction. Table 4 presents results of individual models and the ensemble. Table 5 compares methods on proteins without homologs. Table 6 compares SPOT-Contact-Single, SSCpred, and ESM-1b on CASP14-FM.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a single-sequence contact map predictor using ESM-1b attention maps. 2. The strongest evidence is the 48.7% F1-score improvement over TrRosetta on Neff=1 proteins. 3. The future path involves using more advanced architectures like Transformers.
